mcqs.learning_point: Understand the cell as the basic unit of life
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements best describes why a cell is considered the basic unit of life?

options.A: It can exist independently and perform all life processes.
options.B: It is the smallest part of an organism that can carry out all functions of life.
options.C: It is the smallest particle that can be seen with the naked eye.
options.D: It is the building block of tissues only.

mcqs.answer: It is the smallest part of an organism that can carry out all functions of life.
mcqs.explanation: A cell is the smallest structural and functional unit that can independently perform all vital activities such as metabolism, growth, and reproduction. Option B captures this definition. Option A is partially true but not all cells can exist independently. Options C and D are inaccurate descriptions of the cell's role.

mcqs.learning_point: State the basic ideas of cell theory
mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three main statements of the cell theory?

options.A: All living organisms are composed of one or more cells.
options.B: The cell is the basic unit of structure and function in living organisms.
options.C: All cells arise only from pre‑existing cells.
options.D: Cells can spontaneously generate from non‑living matter.

mcqs.answer: Cells can spontaneously generate from non‑living matter.
mcqs.explanation: The three core statements of cell theory are: (1) all living things are made of cells, (2) the cell is the basic unit of life, and (3) all cells arise from pre‑existing cells. Spontaneous generation (option D) was disproved and is not part of the theory. Options A, B, and C are correct statements of the theory.

mcqs.question: Which characteristic distinguishes a multicellular organism from a unicellular organism?

options.C: Having more than one cell that are specialized for different functions.

mcqs.answer: Having more than one cell that are specialized for different functions.
mcqs.explanation: Multicellular organisms consist of many cells that often differentiate to perform specific tasks, whereas unicellular organisms consist of a single cell that carries out all life processes. The presence of a nucleus (A) and photosynthesis (B) are not exclusive to multicellular life, and mobility (D) is not a defining feature.

mcqs.question: The presence of many mitochondria in a cell most directly supports which function?
mcqs.explanation: Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell; they generate ATP through cellular respiration, providing energy for cellular activities. Protein synthesis occurs in ribosomes (A), genetic material is stored in the nucleus (C), and immune protection involves lysosomes and other mechanisms (D).

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the cell as the basic unit of life
mcqs.question: A scientist isolates a single yeast cell and observes it growing and dividing into a colony. Which observation best supports the idea that the cell is the basic unit of life?

options.A: The colony changes color over time.
options.B: The single cell can carry out metabolism, growth, and reproduction on its own.
options.C: The cell requires other cells to survive.
options.D: The colony produces spores only when in contact with other colonies.

mcqs.answer: The single cell can carry out metabolism, growth, and reproduction on its own.
mcqs.explanation: The ability of an isolated cell to perform all vital processes—metabolism, growth, and division—demonstrates that the cell itself is the fundamental unit of life. Color change (A) is a secondary observation, while C and D contradict the definition of a basic unit.

mcqs.learning_point: State the basic ideas of cell theory
mcqs.question: A student claims that new cells can appear spontaneously in a sterile broth. Which statement should the student refer to in order to refute this claim?

options.A: All living organisms are made of cells.
options.B: Cells are the basic unit of life.
options.C: All cells arise only from pre‑existing cells.

mcqs.answer: All cells arise only from pre‑existing cells.
mcqs.explanation: The third tenet of cell theory explicitly states that cells originate only from existing cells, disproving spontaneous generation. Options A and B are true but do not directly address the claim. Option D is unrelated to the origin of cells.

mcqs.question: A common misconception is that all bacteria are unicellular because they are microscopic. Which statement correctly addresses this misconception?

options.A: All bacteria are unicellular, so the statement is true.
options.B: Some bacteria form multicellular filaments, so size alone does not determine unicellularity.
options.D: Microscopic size automatically means an organism is unicellular.

mcqs.answer: Some bacteria form multicellular filaments, so size alone does not determine unicellularity.
mcqs.explanation: While most bacteria are unicellular, certain species (e.g., cyanobacteria) can arrange into filamentous or colonial forms, showing that microscopic size is not the sole criterion. Options A and C are absolute statements that are incorrect, and D is a false generalisation.

mcqs.question: Why do plant cells have a large central vacuole, whereas animal cells usually have many small vacuoles?

options.A: Large vacuole stores water and maintains turgor pressure, essential for plant rigidity; animal cells do not need turgor pressure.
options.B: Large vacuole produces energy for the plant cell; animal cells generate energy in mitochondria.
options.C: Large vacuole contains DNA; animal cells keep DNA in nucleus.
options.D: Large vacuole is for photosynthesis; animal cells lack chloroplasts.

mcqs.answer: Large vacuole stores water and maintains turgor pressure, essential for plant rigidity; animal cells do not need turgor pressure.
mcqs.explanation: The central vacuole in plant cells functions mainly in water storage and generating turgor pressure, which keeps the plant upright. Animal cells lack this requirement and therefore have several smaller vacuoles for storage and transport. Options B, C, and D describe functions not performed by vacuoles.
